en-US.title: Venture: History Nearby
en-US.subtitle: The history of where you stand
en-US.promoText: Find out what happened where you're standing: the ships, palaces, plaques and vanished places within a walk of you, each told in about a minute.
en-US.description:
Find out what happened where you're standing.

Most of what happened where you live left nothing you would notice. A prison that stood for two centuries. A palace that burned down. The reason a street bends the way it does. Venture puts those stories back on the ground they belong to, in order of how far you would have to walk.

FINDING

Stories are listed nearest first, each with a photograph so you know it when you see it, and the one detail that makes it worth the walk. A nuclear reactor ran in Greenwich until 1996. Henry VIII was baptized down the road.

Some of it is still standing. Some of it is a car park now — and a vanished palace still has a location, so Venture will still take you to the spot where it stood.

READING AND LISTENING

Every place gets a short account, about a minute long, that opens with the thing you would repeat to someone else rather than the earliest date it can find. Read it, or put the phone in your pocket and listen while you walk. Larger areas get a longer telling in parts, with a timeline and the other stories standing on the same ground.

WALKING THERE

A compass gives you a bearing and a distance and nothing else, which is usually all you want. When you would rather be led, Go follows a walking route with turn-by-turn directions. Times are estimates, so trust the signs and what is in front of you.

KEEPING

Save whatever is worth coming back to, and download it to read where there is no signal — underground, or abroad. Venture remembers what you have already read and where you have stood, so returning to an area shows you what is new rather than what you have seen.

BEFORE YOU GO

You do not have to be there. Search anywhere — the town you are visiting next week, the street you grew up on — and read it from an armchair.

Coverage is richest in Britain, and thins as you go further out and further into open country.

THE SMALL PRINT

No account, no advertising, nothing tracking you. Your location is used on your phone to sort what is near you and to point the compass, and it goes no further.
